headline: Ukraine says public air raid alert app sent false alerts after being hacked
description: False alerts appeared in Kyiv and other areas before app was taken offline
author: Reuters
article_text:
Ukraine’s Air Force said on Sunday that the public ​air raid alert app had been ‌hacked.

The app for a short time showed Kyiv and other areas subject to nuclear and chemical ​alerts and the threat of street ​combat. An erroneous message said Russia’s hypersonic ⁠Oreshnik missile had been deployed.

“The air ​alert app appears to have been subjected to ​enemy influence,” the air force said on Telegram. “There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our ​updates on our channel!”

The abnormality later ​disappeared.

Ukraine’s Ministry for Digital Transformation said the app was ‌not ⁠in operation, but other means of alerting the public were functioning, as were air raid sirens.

In a separate event, the mobile ​app of Russia’s ​emergencies ⁠ministry was hit by a massive cyberattack that resulted in the ​spread of false information to the ​public, ⁠state news agency TASS quoted the ministry as saying early on Monday.

It was not ⁠immediately clear ​whether the two incidents ​were linked.

headline: Bangladesh garment factories reopen amid wage unrest
description: Manufacturers warn of more disruption as workers demand minimum wage of 30,000 taka
author: Reuters
article_text:
Bangladesh’s garment factories reopened on Monday after widespread closures and production disruptions a day earlier, but manufacturers remain concerned about further unrest over workers’ demands for higher wages.

The ready-made garment sector accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh’s export earnings, employs about 4 million workers and contributes around 10% to ​gross domestic product.

The latest unrest disrupted operations in key manufacturing hubs and raised concerns over export ​shipments and buyer confidence in Bangladesh, the world’s second-largest apparel exporter after China, as ⁠workers demanded a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($243), up from 12,500 taka.

The demand reflects mounting pressure ​from rising living costs and persistent inflation.

The government formed a six-member minimum wage board on Sunday to review ​the demand, but the move failed to immediately quell unrest.

Workers set up road blockades in several industrial areas on Sunday, with police in the capital Dhaka using tear gas and water cannons to disperse protesters.

“Bangladesh has among the lowest garment wages ​in the world,” said Babul Akhter, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garment and Industrial Workers Federation and ​a workers’ representative on the wage board.

“If factory owners cannot pay workers properly, they should negotiate better prices with international ‌buyers. They ⁠cannot build a business on the backs of underpaid workers.”

No work, no pay

Factory owners said the industry faces higher costs, energy market uncertainty linked to conflict in the Middle East and slowing demand in key export markets.

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said demonstrations in multiple cities disrupted operations at 529 factories and ​affected nearly 1 million ​workers.

“The government has already ⁠taken a step by forming the wage board. We expect workers to allow the review process to proceed,” said BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan.

“If protests break out ​later in the day and we are forced to shut factories, we will ​have no option ⁠but to invoke the ‘no work, no pay’ provision,” he said, adding that industry representatives were scheduled to meet the home minister to discuss the unrest.

Selim Raihan, an economics professor at the University of Dhaka, said workers’ demands were ⁠understandable given ​high inflation, and suppressed wages could cause further unrest.

However, he ​cautioned that a substantial wage increase could raise production costs, squeeze exporters’ profit margins and weaken Bangladesh’s price competitiveness.

“A phased wage adjustment, improved ​productivity and fairer pricing from international buyers are essential to balancing workers’ welfare with industrial sustainability.”

headline: Pakistan, China set to deepen strategic ties during senior CPC official's visit
description: Liu Haixing's visit aims to strengthen Pakistan-China cooperation
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan is hosting a senior Chinese Communist Party official on Monday for talks aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation, as the two countries seek to expand their longstanding strategic partnership.

Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, is visiting Pakistan for the first time on an official invitation from Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

According to Pakistan’s Foreign Ministry, Liu will meet the country’s leadership and co-chair a high-level event with Dar in Islamabad.

“The visit forms part of the ongoing high-level and party-to-party exchanges between Pakistan and China, reflecting the two countries’ shared commitment to further strengthening their All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership,” the ministry said.

China is Pakistan’s largest trading partner and a key strategic ally. Both countries maintain close cooperation in trade, defence, infrastructure and regional security.

The visit comes days after Pakistan and China established an 18-outlet news exchange network and a dedicated fact-checking mechanism under a newly launched information corridor, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said.

The corridor’s business component has also opened its first regional office in Karachi. Its think-tank component, led by the Pakistan-China Institute, will connect research institutions from both countries for joint discussions, research and publications.

China has pledged more than $65 billion in investment in Pakistan through road, infrastructure and development projects under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

Several Chinese private-sector manufacturers have also entered joint ventures in Pakistan.

The International Department of the CPC Central Committee manages the party’s relations with political parties and organisations worldwide and conducts foreign exchanges to support China’s international engagement.

headline: China's 'Hollywood' turns visitors into stars with immersive drama experience
description: Tourists are paying to dress up and film their own historical dramas at Hengdian Studios
author: Reuters
article_text:
Onlookers ‌craned their necks outside an ornate palace chamber, peering through the doors at four women in silk robes and jade hairpins acting out a court intrigue.

One consort slapped another across the face, the director called for another take, and the cast huddled over ​their phones. Then they started laughing.

But the scene was not for a television drama.

The women were friends who ​had travelled more than 1,500 km to star in their own production at ⁠Hengdian World Studios, the sprawling complex in eastern China known as “China’s Hollywood”, where many of the country’s period dramas ​are filmed.

The studio has expanded into experiential tourism, allowing visitors to shoot their own scenes on sets ranging from ​a replica of Beijing’s Forbidden City to old Shanghai streets used in professional productions.

Since the experience launched in August, Hengdian said more than 2,000 people had taken part, with bookings full on most days, particularly during weekends and holidays.

“During the National Day holiday, I ​shoot from morning until dark, and there are still guests we can’t fit in,” said Wang Weili, a ​director who once filmed 20 groups in a single day.

The attraction reflects a broader shift in Chinese consumer spending.

headline: Netanyahu pressing Trump for Iran nuclear attack: Report
description: US commentator Tucker Carlson says Netanyahu is trying to protect his political future
author: Web Desk
article_text:
US political commentator Tucker Carlson has claimed that President Donald Trump could be days away from authorising a nuclear strike on Iran, alleging that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressing Washington to attack a suspected nuclear site in central Iran.

In a post on X late Sunday, Carlson identified the potential target as Pickaxe Mountain, where Israeli intelligence believes Iran has resumed its nuclear enrichment programme.

He claimed conventional US weapons could not penetrate the estimated 300 feet of solid granite protecting underground tunnels at the site, leaving a nuclear strike as the only military option.

“Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day,” Carlson quoted an unnamed source as saying.

Carlson alleged that Netanyahu was seeking renewed military action to protect his political future, claiming the Israeli prime minister needed Trump’s support to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset and avoid losing power, facing investigations and possible imprisonment.

He further claimed Netanyahu had been pressing senior US officials, including Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper, to resume major combat operations.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe were also allegedly following Netanyahu’s lead, he said.

Carlson warned that renewed fighting could have severe regional and global consequences, saying eight months of conflict had already hurt Gulf economies and disrupted energy and fertiliser markets.

He also claimed 11 of the world’s approximately 850 oil supertankers were badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October.

He warned that a nuclear explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Gulf and threaten the water supply of around 100 million people.

Carlson alleged that the Trump administration had quietly revised US nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called battlefield nuclear weapons easier.

He said Trump could decide by November 7 whether to authorise their use.

Vance, Witkoff favour diplomacy

Carlson claimed Vice President JD Vance and US special envoy Steve Witkoff were urging Trump to pursue a diplomatic agreement with Tehran rather than resume military action.

He said people who had spoken with Iranian decision-makers believed there was a consensus that further conflict would benefit no one and that an agreement was worth pursuing.

He also alleged that Netanyahu had secretly travelled to Abu Dhabi on September 27 to seek UAE support for a final attack on Iran, but Emirati officials had refused.

Carlson further claimed former US president Barack Obama opposed the Iran peace agreement being drafted in Doha.

Trump says sites could be struck within minutes

Carlson’s claims followed Trump’s remarks at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday that one or two Iranian nuclear facilities remained potential targets and could be struck within 10 minutes.

Trump specifically mentioned Pickaxe Mountain, saying the US had military plans for the area, but did not indicate that a nuclear strike had been authorised.

headline: Draft proposal to end Iran-US war circulates after Doha talks
description: Iranian negotiators leave Qatar; follow-up meeting possible as Tehran pushes for deal
author: Reuters
article_text:
Iranian negotiators have left talks with Qatari mediators aimed at ending the war with the United States, ​and a draft proposal is being circulated, with a follow-up meeting ‌possible, an official briefed on the talks said on Monday.

The negotiators departed on Sunday, though not because of difficulties in the negotiations, the official said, without providing further details on the ​draft proposal.

Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson said the basis of the talks is ​a seven-step plan Iran drew up in September to reopen the ⁠Strait of Hormuz and end the US naval blockade on Iran, with Tehran ​now suggesting that proposal could be implemented on a faster timeline under a deal.

The ​spokesperson, Esmaeil Baghaei, said deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi had been in Doha to facilitate the exchange of messages with Washington via Qatari intermediaries.

“Our demands have been articulated very clearly and transparently. ​These demands are reasonable and logical: no final agreement can be initiated, nor ​can the Strait of Hormuz be reopened or secured, unless the US naval blockade is brought ‌to ⁠an end, Iran’s demands are respected, and Iran’s legitimate requirements are addressed,” Baghaei said.

On Saturday, Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera quoted Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi as saying that under a deal the Strait of Hormuz could be opened within a two-day ​timeline rather than ​within the seven ⁠days originally envisaged.

“Iran’s initial proposal was rejected by US President Donald Trump.”

The latest round of diplomacy comes amid concerns that the ​conflict could escalate again after Tuesday’s midterm elections in the ​United States. ⁠Asked about Tehran’s view on the midterms, Baghaei said Tehran did not expect elections to “give birth to a new US.”

headline: PTV plans to revive film and drama academy with modern training facilities
description: Initiative aims to equip young people with professional skills and strengthen Pakistan’s creative industry
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Monday directed the formulation of a comprehensive strategy to revive the Pakistan Television (PTV) Drama and Film Academy as a modern training institution, equipping young people with professional skills in filmmaking, drama production and digital content creation.

He was chairing a high-level meeting to review plans for the revival of the PTV Drama and Film Academy and the revamping of PTV Home through specialised training programmes, modern technical facilities and practical, industry-oriented training models.

Federal Secretary for Information Ashfaq Ahmed Khalil and senior officials of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting attended the meeting.

During the meeting, various training models proposed in collaboration with the private sector were reviewed, with a focus on providing hands-on professional training to young people while creating new revenue streams for Pakistan Television.

The minister said the revival of the PTV Drama and Film Academy and revamping of PTV Home were part of the government’s commitment to promoting the media and creative industries in the country.

He said Pakistan was launching, for the first time, an advanced training programme in colour grading, adding that previously, professionals had to travel abroad to acquire training and access modern facilities in this specialised field.

The availability of advanced colour-grading facilities in Pakistan would provide the film industry and private sector with access to modern technical training and resources, while helping improve the quality of local filmmaking, he added.

The minister directed that a transparent and practical pilot project be launched in partnership with the private sector to ensure that training programmes remained aligned with the evolving needs of the industry.

He said all necessary measures would be taken to make the PTV Academy an effective and fully functional institution in line with modern requirements.

“Equipping young people with practical skills in filmmaking, drama production, editing, colour grading and digital content creation is among our key priorities,” he said.

The meeting also reviewed proposals for establishing modern classrooms and studio laboratories, installing workstations for students, appointing technical staff and trainers, and developing a comprehensive curriculum.

The minister said students would be trained in a professional environment equipped with modern editing suites, studio laboratories and technical equipment.

He emphasised that the training programmes would focus not only on theoretical knowledge but also on practical assignments, project development and portfolio building to enhance the professional capabilities of participants.

He further said young people’s creative projects would be encouraged for PTV News, PTV Home and other Pakistan Television platforms, providing emerging talent with opportunities to showcase their skills.

The initiatives would help strengthen Pakistan’s film and drama industry by developing a skilled workforce, introducing advanced technical expertise and making modern production facilities available locally, he added.

The minister said efforts would also be made to ensure the financial sustainability of the PTV Academy alongside its transformation into an effective professional training centre.

headline: 7m children targeted in anti-polio drives across KP, Balochistan
description: Vaccination campaigns cover 27 districts in KP and 31 in Balochistan; 29,000 teams deployed
author: Web Desk | APP
article_text:
An anti-polio campaign has been launched across 27 designated districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with a coverage target of 4.8 million children under the age of five, sources said on Monday.

According to a Polio Emergency Operation Centre in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, approximately 4.8 million children under the age of five will be administered polio drops during this campaign.

The initiative will commence simultaneously across all districts within the Peshawar, Kohat, Bannu, and Dera Ismail Khan divisions, as well as in the districts of Bajaur, Upper Dir, Lower Dir, Upper Chitral, Lower Chitral, Abbottabad, Torghar, Lower Kohistan, Upper Kohistan, and Kolai Palas.

The campaign will last for seven days in the districts of Peshawar and Khyber, while it will continue for four days in the remaining districts.

A total of 20,772 teams of polio workers have been constituted, comprising 18,630 mobile teams, 1,225 fixed teams, and 917 transit teams to ensure the target.

Furthermore, 4,734 area in-charges have been deployed to ensure effective supervision of the polio teams.

To guarantee the security of the polio teams, approximately 30,000 security personnel will also be deployed across these districts, ensuring complete protection for the polio workers throughout the duration of the campaign.

Anti-polio campaign in Balochistan

A seven-day anti-polio campaign began in 31 districts of Balochistan on Monday, targeting more than 2.2 million children for vaccination.

According to the Emergency Operations Centre (EOC), 8,888 teams have been formed to administer polio drops during the campaign.

The EOC said no polio case had been reported in Balochistan since November 2024.

headline: Trump makes final appeal for support ahead of midterms
description: President urges voters to preserve the party’s control of Congress in Tuesday’s elections
author: Web Desk
article_text:
US President Donald Trump held his final campaign rallies in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday, making a last appeal for Republican support ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress.

Speaking first in Dubuque, Iowa, and later in Salina, Kansas, Trump urged voters to give Republicans another two years in control of both chambers of Congress, saying this would allow his administration to continue pursuing its agenda.

He told supporters in Salina that a Republican victory in the House of Representatives and Senate would ensure that his administration continued to put America first.

Trump used the rallies to highlight his proposed priorities, including tougher immigration controls, requirements for voter identification and proof of citizenship, and a nationwide ban on sanctuary cities.

He also advocated capital punishment for major drug traffickers, human traffickers and anyone convicted of killing a law enforcement officer.

Describing what he called a golden age for the United States, Trump urged supporters to turn out on election day and help Republicans secure victory.

In Kansas, he also threw his support behind Republican Senator Roger Marshall, who is seeking another term, and gubernatorial candidate Ty Masterson, calling on voters to back both candidates.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio joined Trump briefly at the Salina rally, crediting the president with strengthening national security. He said the country was safer and its adversaries weaker under Trump’s leadership.

The November 3 elections will determine the balance of power in Congress, with all 435 seats in the House and 35 Senate seats being contested.

headline: Lindsay Clancy returns to Massachusetts court for hearing that could shape potential murder retrial
description: Jury deadlocked in first trial over killing her children
author: Reuters
article_text:
Lindsay Clancy is ​due back in court on Monday for a hearing that could determine whether she will be retried ‌for killing her three young children at her Massachusetts home in 2023 after a jury deadlocked at her first trial.

Judge William Sullivan is scheduled to hear arguments in Plymouth, Massachusetts, on Clancy’s bid to dismiss the murder charges and to discuss a timetable for a potential ​new trial if he allows the case to proceed.

Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz’s office has yet ​to publicly detail its plans for a retrial of Clancy, 36. She faces first-degree murder ⁠charges over the deaths of her daughter Cora, 5; son Dawson, 3; and 8-month-old son Callan.

In a filing last ​week, prosecutors urged Sullivan to reject a defence bid to have the case thrown out, saying they “should be permitted to ​continue to pursue justice for Cora, Dawson and Callan Clancy.”

Sullivan at a September 29 hearing said the parties should be prepared on Monday to discuss a date for a retrial.

No one at Clancy’s initial trial disputed that she strangled her three children with exercise bands on ​January 24, 2023, in the basement of their home in the Boston suburb of Duxbury. She then cut herself ​with a knife and jumped from a second-story window in an attempt to end her own life, leaving her paralysed.

Her lawyers, though, ‌have argued ⁠the evidence showed Clancy was in the throes of postpartum psychosis at the time and should be found not guilty by reason of insanity, known in Massachusetts as lack of criminal responsibility.

Some of the jurors in televised interviews later said that but for one holdout juror, they had been prepared to find Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity. Such ​a verdict would have resulted ​in her commitment to ⁠a state psychiatric hospital, subject to regular court review.

Prosecutors have several options before them, including retrying Clancy on the first-degree murder charges or seeking her conviction on lesser second-degree murder ​charges, which would give her the option to waive a jury trial and proceed ​before a judge.

A ⁠first-degree murder conviction carries a mandatory sentence of life without parole. Second-degree murder allows for the possibility of parole.

Defence lawyers are expected on Monday to argue that a retrial would violate Clancy’s constitutional protection against being tried twice for the same ⁠crime, known ​as double jeopardy.

They contend the mistrial declared on September 4 was ​unnecessary. Citing jury notes that stated the holdout juror was not following the law on reasonable doubt despite the judge’s instructions, defence lawyers say Sullivan ​should have instead questioned the holdout and potentially removed the juror.

headline: Six family members killed in Hangu house shooting
description: Victims include two women, three children and a man; police launch search operation for suspect, who is the family head’s nephew
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
At least six members of a family were killed in a shooting inside a house in Hangu district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Monday, police said.

The incident took place in the Sarokhel area within the jurisdiction of Doaba police station.

District Police Officer Salahuddin Kundi said the victims included two women, three children and a man. Police shifted the bodies to Doaba Hospital.

According to the DPO, the suspected shooter is the nephew of the head of the household, Noor Rehman.

He said the suspect is reportedly a drug addict and that his uncle had repeatedly stopped him from bringing friends with similar habits to the house.

Police personnel reached the scene shortly after receiving information about the incident.

Authorities have launched an investigation to determine the circumstances and motive behind the shooting. A search operation is also underway to arrest the suspect.

headline: LPG shipments arrive at Port Qasim, raising hopes of price relief
description: A total of 4,816 tonnes of LPG is expected to reach Karachi in the first week of November as two vessels bring fresh supplies
author: Syed Safdar Abbas
article_text:
Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) shipments continue to arrive at Port Qasim, with fresh supplies expected to ease prices across the country.

The first vessel, Alisa, has berthed at the SSGC terminal and is transferring 3,071 tonnes of LPG, according to LPG Marketing Association Chairman Ali Haider.

Another cargo vessel, Atran, carrying 1,745 metric tonnes of LPG from Oman, is scheduled to berth at the port on Monday.

With the arrival of the two shipments, a total of 4,816 tonnes of LPG will have reached Karachi during the first week of November.

Ali Haider said the increased arrivals could bring down LPG prices across the country.

LPG is currently selling for Rs500 to Rs550 per kilogram in Karachi.

headline: Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if US agrees to demands
description: Tehran says offer shows ‘good faith’ as Trump warns Iran to expect ‘the hammer’ at midterm rally
author: AFP
article_text:
Iran on Monday said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington agrees to conditions, as US President Donald Trump issued his latest war threat at a rally for midterm elections.

A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed “good faith”.

Tehran has blockaded Hormuz since the war started in February, sending energy prices soaring and posing an electoral challenge for Trump. The narrow gateway to the energy-rich Gulf normally carries one-fifth of global oil consumption.

“The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.

“We have stated that, if Iran’s demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period.”

In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz if the US agreed to demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Baqaei said messages were being exchanged with the United States via mediators, adding that “everything depends” on the US side accepting the Iranian demands.

“Only then can we discuss the subsequent stages.”

During final rallies for the US midterms on Tuesday, where diesel prices and consumer inflation are a key issue, Trump struck a belligerent tone, warning Iran to expect “the hammer”.

“The only reason why I’m not finished with Iran is I want to be nice. I want to try and save all those lives if I can… But at some point we’re going to have to give them the hammer,” he told voters in Iowa.

‘Prevent war entirely’

Officials from Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Turkey have held talks with Iran in recent days, while US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Tehran.

Oman’s ruler Sultan Haitham bin Tariq discussed the war with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a visit to Beijing on Monday, an Omani foreign ministry statement said.

“The two sides called for resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, urging the United States and Iran to pursue a peaceful path, achieve a ceasefire (and) prevent war entirely,” it said, calling for “dialogue and negotiations as soon as possible”.

China’s top diplomat also told a senior Iranian official that Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security”.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi made the remarks to Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a statement from Beijing.

“All parties should… in a spirit of reason and pragmatism, focus on a political solution rather than once again resorting to armed conflict,” Wang was cited as saying.

Bagheri told Wang that “Tehran’s stance on defending its national security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity remains unchanged, and that Iran will make no compromises in this regard”, according to state TV.

‘Powerful response’

In an interview with Al Jazeera released on Sunday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transiting the strait.

He said the US must also remove sanctions imposed in recent months and reduce American troop numbers in the region.

Washington has since August rolled out a fresh raft of sanctions, part of what it called “economic asphyxiation” of Iran.

Trump’s “hammer” comment is just the latest threat to Tehran from the US and Israel, whose joint attack marked the start of the war on February 28.

On Saturday, Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets including Pickaxe mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

“Any act of aggression against Iran, any military attack against Iran, by whatever means, will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response from us,” Baqaei said.

At the midterms, Democrats expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on Trump for the first time in two years.

article_text:
Pakistan’s headline inflation eased to 9.6% year-on-year (YoY) in October 2026, down from 10.3% in September, according to data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Monday.

The Consumer Price Index (CPI) stood at 6.2% in October 2025.

On a month-on-month (MoM) basis, inflation rose 1.1% in October, compared with 1.3% in September and 1.7% in October 2025.

Urban inflation eased to 9.5% YoY in October from 10.1% in September. It stood at 6% in October 2025.

On a monthly basis, urban inflation increased 0.8% in October, compared with 1.3% in September and 1.4% in October last year.

Rural inflation stood at 9.8% YoY in October, down from 10.5% in September but up from 6.6% in October 2025.

On a MoM basis, rural inflation rose 1.5% in October, compared with 1.2% in September and 2.1% in October last year.

During the first four months of FY27, average CPI inflation reached 10.05%, compared with 4.79% in the corresponding period last year.

Finance ministry outlook

The finance ministry had projected inflation in the range of 9.5% to 10.5% for October, citing elevated energy and food prices in Pakistan in line with global trends.

In its Monthly Economic Update and Outlook for October 2026, the ministry said the inflation outlook would remain sensitive to international energy prices, food supplies and base effects.

It also described the domestic economic outlook for FY27 as promising, with the recovery expected to draw support from improving crop prospects, selected manufacturing industries, construction activity and expanding external earnings.

Market expectations

Several brokerage houses had projected October inflation at around 9% to 9.5%, although rising fuel and electricity costs were expected to sustain price pressures and complicate the central bank’s monetary policy outlook.

Topline Securities projected CPI inflation at 9% to 9.5% YoY in October, compared with 10.26% in September and 6.25% in October 2025.

The brokerage also warned that average inflation could exceed 9% in FY27 if international oil prices remained between $100 and $110 per barrel, compared with its earlier forecast of 8.5% to 9%.

Meanwhile, Insight Securities estimated October inflation at 9.3%, compared with 10.3% in September and 6.2% in the corresponding month last year.

headline: China FM tells Iran official Beijing supports 'safeguarding sovereignty'
description: Wang Yi urges ‘political solution’ over ‘armed conflict’ as Iran’s Bagheri Kani makes unannounced Beijing visit
author: AFP
article_text:
China’s top diplomat told a senior Iranian official that Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security” as they met in the Chinese capital on Monday, after threats of renewed US strikes.

President Donald Trump said on Saturday that the United States has knocked out much of Iran’s military but still has to “take care of” one or two targets, as Tehran warned of reprisals if attacked.

“China supports Iran in safeguarding its own sovereignty and security,” Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri Kani, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a statement from Beijing.

The foreign ministry had not previously announced the visit by Bagheri Kani to Beijing.

“All parties should… in a spirit of reason and pragmatism, focus on a political solution rather than once again resorting to armed conflict,” Wang told Bagheri Kani, according to the statement.

China, a top economic partner of Iran, has long sought a detente in the months-long conflict in the Middle East, which has at times spilt over into neighbouring countries.

This month, China will send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia as part of “shuttle diplomacy visits… aimed at promoting peace talks (and) easing tensions”, a ministry spokesperson told a regular news briefing.

Also on Monday, Chinese President Xi Jinping met the Sultan of Oman for talks in Beijing — the first visit to China by the Gulf nation’s head of state since diplomatic ties were established.

Xi told Haitham bin Tariq that China was ready to “contribute to peace, stability and prosperity in the region”.

The Chinese leader also said that the Middle East should not become a “wrestling ground for major-country rivalry and geopolitical conflicts”, state news agency Xinhua reported.

headline: Govt seeks Rs15/litre petrol discount from refineries
description: Ali Pervaiz Malik says global energy price hikes have increased economic and transportation costs
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The government has sought cooperation from oil refineries to provide petrol at a discount of Rs15 per litre as part of its efforts to protect consumers from rising global energy prices.

Speaking at a press conference alongside Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar in Islamabad, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said rising international energy prices had affected Pakistan’s economy and increased transportation costs.

He said providing relief to the public remained among the government’s top priorities and that it had launched a fuel subsidy scheme to support consumers.

Millions of people are benefiting from the scheme, Malik said, adding that the government had also requested cooperation from oil refineries to provide petrol at a discount of Rs15 per litre.

He said the government would move forward transparently, keeping the public interest in mind.

Tarar said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s mission was to minimise the financial burden on the public.

He said Pakistan’s economy, like those of other countries, had been affected by the global situation.

The government had launched the subsidy scheme to provide relief to owners of motorcycles, Qingqi rickshaws and small cars, he added.

More than 15 million people have benefited from the fuel subsidy scheme, while the government has provided relief worth Rs27 billion under the programme, Tarar said.

He added that relevant government departments had worked together to implement the scheme.

headline: OpenAI partners with state oil firm among raft of UAE deals
description: ADNOC, OpenAI and G42 partner at ADIPEC as the UAE pushes to diversify its economy away from energy
author: AFP
article_text:
UAE state oil company ADNOC on Monday announced a partnership with OpenAI, saying it would be the world’s first energy firm to deploy OpenAI Frontier, an advanced artificial intelligence platform.

The deal was among a raft of agreements announced with the UAE as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman attended its flagship oil industry event in Abu Dhabi, which has bet heavily on the technology in a bid to diversify its economy away from energy.

Gulf countries have been struggling to export oil since Iran began blockading the Strait of Hormuz and targeting tankers in the area, but the US military has been escorting ships through the route.

The blockade has caused a spike in oil prices.

ADNOC said in a statement that OpenAI’s models would enable it to be “the first energy company in the world to use this technology to value every barrel while it is still in the ground”.

The deal will also see ADNOC and OpenAI partner with G42, an Emirati AI company.

No financial details of the deal were disclosed.

Altman met with Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed al-Nahyan, signing a number of agreements to incorporate AI into government institutions, investment funds and companies.

The Abu Dhabi government and OpenAI were launching “the world’s first AI-native Machine-Readable Government initiative”, the emirate’s media office said in a statement.

The initiative will enable “AI-powered systems to assist officials with routine regulatory compliance assessments, including those related to issuing permits and certificates”, it added.

A pilot is already in production with the Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority focused on food imports, the statement said.

State-backed fund Mubadala, OpenAI and Inception42, part of G42, also signed a deal to apply advanced AI capabilities to “investment analysis, opportunity identification and risk assessment”, as well as a five-year agreement to adopt Frontier AI “across government, enterprise and education”.

‘Forward-looking’

The oil-rich UAE is a top AI player in the Middle East and has been seeking to become a dominant force in the field globally.

“From the moment ChatGPT was born, the world has asked what energy can do for AI, and now together we will find out what AI can do for energy,” said ADNOC’s managing director and CEO Sultan Al Jaber at the ADIPEC oil conference.

Altman praised the UAE as having “consistently been the most forward-looking country in the world for AI adoption”.

According to the ADNOC statement, “interconnected AI agents will continuously forecast crude oil supply, demand, prices and margins, predict their impacts before they occur, and weigh the commercial and operational impact of every decision as one integrated process”.

The UAE has been betting heavily on AI since 2017, when it named the world’s first AI minister and became the second country after Canada to unveil a national AI strategy.

A year later, G42 was founded with backing from Abu Dhabi-based sovereign wealth fund Mubadala. Chaired by the UAE president’s brother, Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, it offers a range of AI products and employs more than 23,000 people.

Last year, the US approved the export of advanced Nvidia chips to both the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

On Sunday, Saudi state oil firm Aramco said it was taking a 49 per cent stake in Saudi state-backed AI company Humain, injecting cash and assets as the tech firm tries to scale up to meet rising demand.

Aramco, one of the world’s biggest companies by market capitalisation, will inject about 9.9 billion Saudi riyals ($2.6 billion) into Humain this year along with AI, compute and digital assets.

headline: Pakistan, China reaffirm commitment to strengthen strategic partnership
description: Field Marshal Asim Munir and Chinese Minister Liu Haixing discuss bilateral ties, regional security and ways to strengthen strategic cooperation
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Chinese Communist Party official Liu Haixing met Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi, the military’s media wing said on Monday.

According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee (IDCPC), called on the military chief during his visit to Pakistan.

The two sides discussed matters of mutual interest, evolving regional and international security dynamics, and bilateral relations.

They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between Pakistan and China.

Field Marshal Asim Munir highlighted the historic and time-tested ties between the two countries, emphasising the importance of sustained high-level engagement and stronger institutional linkages.

He also stressed the need to expand cooperation across areas of mutual interest.

The Chinese minister appreciated Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability and expressed confidence that the longstanding strategic partnership between the two countries would continue to advance.

The meeting underscored the shared commitment of Pakistan and China to maintaining close strategic ties and strengthening cooperation on regional and international issues.

headline: Adrian Hamilton-Manns takes charge as PIA CEO
description: Adrian brings with him over 30 years of experience and has served as chief executive of three airlines
author: Business Recorder
article_text:
Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has appointed aviation executive Adrian Hamilton-Manns as its new chief executive officer (CEO), with him assuming charge on Monday, November 2, 2026.

The appointment was announced by the PIA Board, which said Hamilton-Manns would lead the national carrier through its ongoing transformation and efforts to improve its commercial viability.

According to the announcement, Hamilton-Manns brings more than 30 years of experience in the global aviation industry and has served as chief executive of three airlines. He is described by the board as an expert in airline transformation and turnaround strategies.

Before his appointment at PIA, he headed Oman-based SalamAir. He previously served as president and CEO of Kazakhstan’s FlyArystan from April 2020 to July 2024 and was the founding CEO of Africa-focused low-cost carrier flyafrica.com from 2012 to 2016.

His previous experience also includes senior commercial positions at India’s IndiGo, South African Airways, Virgin Australia’s Pacific Blue and Indonesia’s Mandala Airlines. He began his aviation career at Air New Zealand in 1997.

Hamilton-Manns takes over the position from Air Vice Marshal (AVM) Amir Hayat, who served as PIA’s CEO for four-and-a-half years.

The PIA Board acknowledged Hayat’s contribution to the airline, particularly his role in introducing structural reforms, improving operational efficiency and preparing the national carrier for privatisation.

“We are immensely grateful for AVM Amir Hayat’s steadfast commitment to the national flag carrier during a highly complex transitional period,” the PIA Board chairman said.

Welcoming the new CEO, the chairman expressed confidence that Hamilton-Manns’ aviation experience would help accelerate the airline’s strategic objectives, improve service standards and achieve sustainable profitability.

The appointment comes as PIA enters a new phase under private-sector management. An Arif Habib-led consortium took over the airline’s management on June 29, 2026, following the privatisation process.

headline: Fazlur Rehman questions federal control of former FATA districts after KP emergency
description: JUI-F chief demands clarity over tribal areas' administrative future and resources, says 2018 merger has failed to deliver promised reforms
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman has questioned the federal government’s administrative arrangements in the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA), demanding clarity over the region’s political future, constitutional rights and natural resources following the imposition of an emergency in 12 districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Addressing a Digital Media and Workers Convention organised by his party in Peshawar, Fazlur Rehman said the concerns of political leaders and tribal residents over the region’s administrative status should be addressed through arguments rather than allegations and character assassination.

The former FATA was merged with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under the 25th Constitutional Amendment in 2018, ending its separate federally administered status.

However, the federal government imposed governor’s rule across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and an emergency in 12 designated districts on October 11, 2026, under Articles 234 and 232 of the Constitution, respectively.

The measures placed provincial government functions under Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and established a separate Area Development Secretariat (ADS) to oversee the 12 districts, including the eight districts carved out of the former FATA.

Fazlur Rehman questioned the arrangements, saying the government must explain the roles of federal authorities, the governor and the newly established administrative structures.

Questions over merger and administrative arrangements

Discussing the 2018 merger, the JUI-F chief claimed that senior figures had told him the decision was wrong and that proposals were being considered to reverse it and restore the tribal areas’ previous administrative status.

He alleged that the original merger had been carried out at the behest of a powerful entity and suggested that similar interests were behind proposals to bring the region back under federal administration.

Fazlur Rehman said the political and constitutional rights of tribal residents had been central to the merger debate, but the present issue was increasingly about the region’s resources and economic interests.

He questioned why a proper administrative system had not been established even 10 years after the merger.

The JUI-F chief said the old system of qanungos and patwaris remained in place, disputes over the division of inherited properties had not been resolved, and the police system had yet to be properly organised.

He argued that past decisions should be assessed in the context of the circumstances prevailing at the time, while current challenges required solutions based on present-day realities.

Raises questions over emergency and governor’s role

Fazlur Rehman also questioned the distribution of administrative powers following the imposition of emergency measures.

He said emergency-related matters were being handled directly by the Interior Ministry, while the prime minister’s direct role in matters concerning governor’s rule had also been mentioned.

He added that a council had been established to oversee routine affairs and issue instructions, raising questions about the governor’s role and the authority of the new administrative setup.

The JUI-F chief demanded an explanation of the constitutional provisions governing the measures, particularly Articles 232 and 234.

He said political and administrative changes must follow constitutional procedures and that disagreements should be resolved within the constitutional framework.

Calls for protection of tribal resources

Fazlur Rehman maintained that tribal residents were being deprived of their economic rights.

He called for transparent agreements between parties possessing natural resources and those providing the technology and expertise to exploit them.

The region’s resources should be treated as the property of its people, he said, stressing that local communities must receive their due economic rights.

Says critics are targeting his household

Responding to criticism against him, Fazlur Rehman alleged that some people were contacting religious scholars and party workers to persuade them to issue statements against him.

He claimed that critics were even searching for corruption in his household kitchen and generator.

He urged political opponents to maintain decency and restraint despite their differences.

The JUI-F chief said he continued to respect those who visited his home and rejected personal allegations and social media criticism as answers to the political questions he had raised.

Referring to Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, he described him as an elder brother and a respectable figure.

Fazlur Rehman said he had merely teased Asif, but the defence minister’s real anger emerged the following day.

Reacting to suggestions that he should move to Afghanistan, the JUI-F chief said he had no personal dispute with anyone and wanted answers to his questions as a Pakistani citizen.

Recalls role in PTI-government negotiations

Fazlur Rehman also discussed his role in negotiations between the government and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), saying he had reservations about some of the party’s demands and its approach during its long march.

He said government representatives subsequently contacted him, while Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also invited him for a meeting.

However, he insisted on open dialogue involving the relevant parties instead of holding a secret meeting.

According to Fazlur Rehman, the prime minister proposed a solution, which he subsequently discussed with PTI leaders along with his own suggestions.

He said there were initially hopes of reaching a consensus, but he later received a telephone call from Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar informing him that the federal cabinet did not agree with the proposals.

Governor’s rule was imposed afterwards, he added.

The JUI-F chief stressed that commitments and dialogue mattered in politics, saying political affairs could not be conducted through false narratives.

He also rejected allegations that his party was sympathetic towards terrorism, arguing that political parties should be allowed to play their role freely.

Fazlur Rehman said his party would not be forced out of politics through pressure or threats, adding that its workers would not be intimidated by such tactics.

He called for a healthy political environment in which disagreements were addressed through democratic and political means.

He called for a healthy political environment in which disagreements were addressed through democratic and political means.

headline: Yemen's Houthis advance to within 80 km of Aden
description: Houthis took Al-Maqatirah district after assault launched three days ago, sources say
author: Reuters
article_text:
Yemen’s Houthis have advanced to ​within 80 km (50 miles) of Aden, the main stronghold and temporary capital of the country’s internationally recognised ‌government, four military sources told Reuters on Monday.

The advance brings the Houthis closer to Aden than at any point since the early months of the war in 2015, when they briefly entered the city before being driven out.

The latest offensive has opened a volatile new front in the wider ​US-Israeli war on Iran, drawing both the Houthis and Saudi Arabia deeper into the regional conflict.

The Houthis have escalated their ​attacks on Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen’s government, while the Saudi-led coalition has responded by stepping ⁠up strikes on Houthi positions in Yemen.

The violence has shattered a 2022 UN-brokered truce that had largely halted major attacks ​in a war that began in 2014, when the Houthis drove the government from Sanaa.

Advance threatens main route

The Houthi push threatens strategic ​positions along the main road linking Aden with the besieged city of Taiz, a vital artery for southwestern Yemen.

It follows a broader offensive that began in September, when the Houthis swept down Yemen’s Red Sea coast and seized territory along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, one of the world’s most ​important shipping lanes and a key route for Saudi oil exports to Asia.

The advance gives the Houthis a chance to ​outflank government forces along the mountain range overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the military sources said. Government troops had expelled Houthi fighters from the ‌area ⁠only weeks ago.

Houthi attacks on Aden, the government’s temporary capital since 2015, have also intensified in recent weeks. The group struck Aden airport on Wednesday after warning people to evacuate, while the presidential palace was also hit in October.

Fighting underway on Monday

Fighting between the Houthis and government forces was underway on Monday at a military camp at the entrance to Tur al-Bahah district, one ​of the main approaches to ​Aden. The camp is about ⁠50 km from the provincial capital of Lahj and 80 km from Aden.

The Houthis launched their assault on government positions in Al-Maqatirah three days ago and have since taken the whole ​district, the sources said. The mountainous area overlooks the road linking Taiz to Aden. The ​Houthis forced government ⁠troops to retreat toward Tur al-Bahah, they said.

Yemen’s information minister did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Houthi official Hamid Rizq posted a video, which Reuters could not immediately verify, of what he said were the group’s fighters entering Souq al-Rabouh in Maqatirah ⁠district.

That route ​has been the last remaining link between government-held territory and Taiz during the ​war.

Taiz, Yemen’s third-largest city, has been encircled since early October, when the Houthis cut its main road south to Aden. The siege has displaced more than ​100,000 people and caused shortages of food, fuel and medicine.

headline: China calls for Mideast dialogue in talks with Iran, Saudi, Oman
description: Beijing to send Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia on “shuttle diplomacy” later this month
author: AFP
article_text:
China stepped up diplomatic efforts on Monday to resolve the Middle East crisis, urging a return to the negotiating table in back-to-back meetings with Iranian, Omani and Saudi officials in Beijing.

The meetings come days after US President Donald Trump issued a fresh war threat more than eight months into the conflict, which was triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran and has at times spilt over into neighbouring countries.

Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security”, Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri Kani, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement.

Wang later called for dialogue to end the conflict “while safeguarding regional energy security and the safety of shipping lanes”, as he met with Saudi National Security Adviser Musaad bin Mohammad al-Aiban.

China, a top economic partner of Iran, has long sought a detente in the months-long conflict that has disrupted global shipping.

Trump said on Saturday that the United States had knocked out much of Iran’s military but still has to “take care of” one or two targets, with Tehran warning of reprisals if attacked.

“All parties should… in a spirit of reason and pragmatism, focus on a political solution rather than once again resorting to armed conflict,” Wang told Bagheri Kani, according to the statement.

China’s foreign ministry had not previously announced the visit by Bagheri Kani to Beijing.

President Xi Jinping also met Oman’s sultan for talks in Beijing on Monday — the first visit to China by the Gulf nation’s head of state since diplomatic ties were established.

Xi told Haitham bin Tariq that China was ready to “contribute to peace, stability and prosperity in the region”.

The Chinese leader said that the Middle East should not become a “wrestling ground for major-country rivalry and geopolitical conflicts”, state news agency Xinhua reported.

Later this month, Beijing will send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia as part of “shuttle diplomacy visits… aimed at promoting peace talks (and) easing tensions”, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson told a news briefing.

headline: PM Shehbaz meets Liu Haixing, discusses ways to deepen bilateral ties
description: PM reaffirms Pakistan's commitment to deepening bilateral ties during meeting with IDCPC minister
author: Radio Pakistan
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday emphasised the importance of sustained political engagement and party-to-party exchanges in further strengthening Pakistan-China relations.

He was talking to Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee (IDCPC), who called on him in Islamabad.

Welcoming Liu Haixing and his delegation, the prime minister reaffirmed that Pakistan and China enjoyed an iron-clad, time-tested and all-weather strategic cooperative partnership.

He said the friendship between the two countries was anchored in mutual trust, respect and deep-rooted bonds between their peoples.

PM Shehbaz appreciated the important role played by the IDCPC in fostering institutional linkages and promoting cooperation between the political leadership of the two countries.

Reaffirming Pakistan’s commitment to working closely with China, he commended the shared focus on advancing cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity, infrastructure development, information technology and agricultural modernisation.

Liu Haixing conveyed the greetings of the Chinese leadership and reaffirmed China’s commitment to further deepening its longstanding friendship with Pakistan.

He appreciated the ongoing momentum in high-level and party-to-party exchanges aimed at further strengthening the friendship between the two countries.

Both sides exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining close coordination and cooperation at bilateral and multilateral forums.

The prime minister also hosted a banquet in honour of the visiting dignitary and the accompanying Chinese delegation.

headline: Thar Block-1 project holds three-day free medical camp for local communities
description: Initiative provides maternal and child healthcare services to hundreds of residents in villages near Islamkot
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Thar Block-1 Integrated Energy Project, developed and operated by Shanghai Electric, has concluded a three-day free medical camp for underserved communities in villages near Islamkot, providing healthcare services to hundreds of local residents.

The camp focused on maternal and child healthcare, with medical teams offering health screenings, antenatal counselling, nutritional assessments, family planning guidance and preventive health advice.

Paediatric specialists also examined children to assess their physical growth, nutritional status, immunisation coverage and developmental milestones.

A spokesperson for the project said the initiative reflected Shanghai Electric’s commitment to improving the well-being of communities living near its operations.

“Our vision at the Thar Block-1 Integrated Energy Project extends beyond power generation and national energy security. True progress is measured by the positive impact we make on local communities,” the spokesperson said.

The spokesperson added that the three-day camp was part of the project’s efforts to promote long-term health and improve the quality of life for women and children in Thar.

Energy project and community development

The Thar Block-1 Integrated Energy Project is part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) energy cooperation framework. Developed and operated by Shanghai Electric, it integrates an open-pit lignite mine with an annual production capacity of 7.8 million tonnes and a coal-fired power plant comprising two 660-megawatt units.

The project uses supercritical power generation technology and has a combined generation capacity of 1,320MW.

According to the company, its electricity supplies power to more than four million households across Pakistan.

Shanghai Electric said it remained committed to combining industrial development with community welfare through initiatives aimed at improving healthcare and social conditions in areas surrounding its operations.

The company operates in power generation equipment, industrial machinery and energy solutions, and says it continues to support infrastructure development alongside community engagement.

headline: Government reduces petrol, diesel prices
description: New rates take effect from November 3; diesel sees a sharper reduction
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The government has reduced the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.76 per litre to Rs395.20 from Rs402.96 and petrol by Rs3.40 per litre to Rs374.51 from Rs377.91, effective November 3, 2026.

According to a press release issued by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) on Monday, the regulator revised the ex-depot prices of petroleum products under the federal government’s petroleum pricing mechanism.

The reduction marks the first cut in petrol prices after the rate had remained unchanged at Rs377.91 per litre in the recent revision on Friday.

OGRA said the price adjustments were necessitated by global developments, including changes in Platts rates, premiums and incidentals.

On Friday, the government increased the price of diesel by Rs2.29 per litre to Rs402.96 from Rs400.67, while keeping petrol unchanged at Rs377.91 per litre.

Oil falls in international market

Meanwhile, international oil prices fell around 6% on Monday as talks between Iranian and Qatari officials on ending the US-Israeli war with Iran raised hopes of easing supply disruptions in the Middle East.

Iran’s president also said the supreme leader had granted the government “certain authorities” regarding peace talks.

Brent crude futures fell $6.78, or 6%, to $106.65 a barrel by 1357 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude declined $6.37, or 6.1%, to $97.75 a barrel.

headline: Iran, US in ‘intensive’ talks to avert return to war
description: Araghchi says Qatar and Pakistan are playing ‘a very active mediating role’ as Iran offers to reopen Hormuz under strict conditions
author: AFP
article_text:
Iran on Monday said “intensive” exchanges were underway with Washington and offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions, as efforts escalated to avert a return to war.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said indirect talks were taking place via mediators. China also urged a return to negotiations, while Iran’s security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Oil prices, sent rocketing by Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz energy corridor, dropped more than six per cent on Monday on optimism over the eight-month-old conflict.

“Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive,” Araghchi said in a video interview with the official IRNA news agency.

“Qatar and Pakistan are playing a very active mediating role in these negotiations.”

The Axios news outlet reported that US Vice President JD Vance had sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks, marking the highest-level move in months.

The redoubled diplomatic push comes ahead of Tuesday’s US midterm elections, where dissatisfaction over the war and higher fuel prices are weighing on US President Donald Trump’s Republicans.

Democrats expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on Trump for the first time in two years.

Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said the messages received from the US were “an acknowledgement of our victory”.

But Trump kept up his threats against Iran, telling a campaign rally that at “some point we’re going to have to give them the hammer”.

‘Good-faith approach’

A senior Iranian official said on Tehran was ready to open Hormuz, the export highway for the energy-rich Gulf, within two days — as long as Washington agrees to its list of demands.

In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the strait if the US agreed to demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

“The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran’s good-faith approach,” foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.

“We have stated that, if Iran’s demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period.”

Baqaei said “everything depends” on the US side accepting the Iranian demands. “Only then can we discuss the subsequent stages,” he added.

Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed the war with Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Beijing on Monday — the first visit to China by the Gulf nation’s head of state since diplomatic ties were established.

“The two sides called for resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, urging the United States and Iran to pursue a peaceful path, achieve a ceasefire (and) prevent war entirely,” an Omani statement said.

China also held meetings with Iranian and Saudi officials in Beijing on Monday.

Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security”, Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement.

Bagheri told Wang that “Tehran’s stance on defending its national security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity remains unchanged, and that Iran will make no compromises in this regard”, according to state TV.

Russian President Putin also spoke with Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei about the war by telephone, Iranian state media said.

‘Powerful response’

In an interview with Al Jazeera released on Sunday, Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transiting the strait.

He said the US must also remove sanctions imposed in recent months and reduce American troop numbers in the region.

Washington has since August rolled out a fresh raft of sanctions, part of what it called “economic asphyxiation” of Iran.

American and Israeli threats to Iran rose in the run-up to the midterms and last week’s elections in Israel, where Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu failed to secure a majority.

On Saturday, Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets, including Pickaxe mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

“Any act of aggression against Iran, any military attack against Iran, by whatever means, will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response from us,” Baqaei said.
